channel.title: Cadence Evidence — PT Research Signal
channel.description: Daily curated physical therapy & rehab research for clinicians. AI-scored signal from 56 sources.

item.title: Structured exercise interventions and survival outcomes in patients with cancer: systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials
item.description: This systematic review and meta-analysis of 21 RCTs (n=3828 for overall survival) found that structured exercise interventions were associated with significant improvements in overall survival (HR 0.77; 95% CI 0.65 to 0.92), disease-free survival (HR 0.83; 95% CI 0.72 to 0.95), reduced all-cause mortality (RR 0.82), and reduced cancer-specific mortality (RR 0.74) in patients with cancer, with moderate certainty of evidence.
item.author: BJSM

item.title: Short-Term Effects of Radial Extracorporeal Shock Wave Therapy in Addition to Physiotherapy on Spasticity, Walking Performance, and Quality of Life in Chronic Stroke: A Sham-Controlled Randomized Trial.
item.description: A 4-week program of radial extracorporeal shock wave therapy (rESWT) combined with physiotherapy significantly improved spasticity (-0.56 MAS; 95% CI -0.77 to -0.35), walking performance (-1.41 s 10MWT; -1.87 to -0.96), motor function, and quality of life in chronic stroke patients with plantar flexor spasticity compared to sham treatment.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: The effect of multimodal sensory therapy in consciousness improvement in patients with acquired brain injury: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
item.description: This systematic review and meta-analysis of 18 studies (884 participants) found that multimodal sensory therapy (MST) significantly improved consciousness levels (SMD, 1.48; 95% CI, 1.04-1.92) and increased the odds of coma emergence (OR, 9.85; 95% CI, 3.86-25.01) in adults with acquired brain injury-related disorders of consciousness.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Do blood flow restriction exercises offer additional benefits when compared to conventional exercises in musculoskeletal rehabilitation? A systematic review and meta-analysis
item.description: This systematic review and meta-analysis of 45 RCTs (1652 participants) found low-certainty evidence that low-load exercise with blood flow restriction (LLE-BFR) was superior to low-load exercise (LLE) for muscle strength (SMD=0.82) and disability (SMD=0.63). Moderate-certainty evidence showed no clear difference between LLE-BFR and high-load exercise (HLE) for muscle strength (SMD=0.08).
item.author: BJSM

item.title: Optimal exercise dose in adults with chronic low back pain disorders: systematic review with dose-response network meta-analysis.
item.description: A systematic review and network meta-analysis of 239 trials found that low to moderate exercise doses were associated with short-term, potentially clinically meaningful improvements in disability and pain intensity for chronic low back pain, with optimal model-predicted doses of 4 sessions/week, 25 min/session over 13 weeks for disability, and 3 sessions/week, 30 min/session over 8 weeks for pain.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Exercise-only interventions and exercise-based multidomain lifestyle interventions to promote cognitive function in older adults without dementia: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 227 studies found that exercise-only interventions significantly improved executive functions, memory, and processing speed in older adults without dementia compared to control. Exercise-plus interventions (exercise combined with other lifestyle interventions) were significantly better than exercise-only for executive functions and processing speed, but not for memory.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Fatigue-related neuromuscular outcomes following ACL reconstruction: a systematic review and meta-analysis
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 17 studies (n=477) found that individuals post-ACL reconstruction showed greater post-fatigue impairments in quadriceps central activation ratio (SMD: -0.69, p < 0.001) and muscle activation patterns (SMD: -0.62, p < 0.001) compared to healthy controls, with moderate-certainty evidence.
item.author: BMC Sports Sci Med Rehabil

item.title: Effects of TENS, NMES, and Combination Therapy on Hemiplegic Shoulder Pain and Function After Stroke.
item.description: This prospective randomized study (n=60) found that combined TENS and NMES significantly reduced hemiplegic shoulder pain and improved SPADI scores more than TENS alone, and also improved shoulder ROM, in acute and subacute stroke patients, when added to a standardized rehabilitation program.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Physical Exercise Reduces Fall-Related Outcomes Among People With Stroke: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 18 studies (1536 participants) found that physical exercise significantly reduced the number of falls by 39% (IRR = 0.61, 95% CI = [0.47, 0.78]) among people with stroke. Balance training and programs integrating cognitive components were most effective, particularly for those in the chronic stage with mild to moderate disability.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Single-bundle versus double-bundle reconstruction in anterior cruciate ligament: a meta-analysis
item.description: A meta-analysis of 41 RCTs (n=3568) found no significant difference in short/long-term KT-1000/2000 side-to-side differences between single-bundle (SB) and double-bundle (DB) ACL reconstruction. DB showed significantly higher negative pivot-shift test rates (OR=0.62, p<0.001 short-term; OR=0.37, p=0.007 long-term) and higher long-term Lysholm scores (MD=-1.32, p=0.004).
item.author: BMC Musculoskelet Disord

item.title: Approach to sarcopenia in older adults: a systematic review of dietary and exercise interventions in the primary care setting
item.description: A systematic review of 6 studies (n=444 in experimental groups) on sarcopenia in older adults found that combined physical exercise and nutritional supplementation in primary care settings demonstrated notable improvements in muscle strength, physical function, and body composition, though results varied with study design and adherence.
item.author: BMC Geriatrics

item.title: Removing barriers to physical activity for people with long-term conditions: co-creating patient-centred guidance through a multistakeholder consensus approach
item.description: This study developed patient-centered, consensus-based digital guidance that offers an alternative to routine medical clearance for people with long-term conditions engaging in organized physical activity. It aims to remove existing barriers by supporting informed, autonomous decision-making through four headline safety statements and seven symptom-specific statements.
item.author: BJSM

item.title: Effect of Music-Based Interventions in Cardiac Rehabilitation: A Systematic Review.
item.description: A systematic review of nine studies on music-based interventions in cardiac rehabilitation found improvements in psychological outcomes, motivation, and exercise adherence, suggesting it as a supportive adjunct rather than a direct cardiovascular outcome modifier.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: REmotely monitored, Mobile health-supported Multidomain Rehabilitation with High Intensity Interval Training for COVID-19 (REMM-HIIT-CoV): Trial Design and Rationale.
item.description: This article outlines the design and rationale for REMM-HIIT-CoV, a multicenter, single-blinded RCT evaluating a remotely monitored, mobile health-supported multidomain rehabilitation program with high-intensity interval training for functional exercise capacity in 140 community-dwelling adults post-COVID-19 hospitalization.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: From evidence to action: a global call to advance sleep health in sport
item.description: This editorial highlights the growing awareness of sleep health in sport but notes that many high-performance environments still operate contrary to healthy sleep and circadian biology, calling for a global, coordinated effort to implement evidence-based sleep health practices.
item.author: BJSM

item.title: Training-related concussions in mens English Premiership Rugby Union: an eight-season prospective cohort study of 153 243 player-weeks
item.description: An eight-season prospective cohort study (153,243 player-weeks) in elite men's English Premiership Rugby Union found a training-related concussion incidence of 0.23 per 1000 hours, with preseason (IRR 1.80) and full-contact training (IRR 2.20) significantly increasing risk compared to the final three months of the season and non-contact training.
item.author: BJSM

item.title: Combinations of stepping intensity and daily step counts against all-cause and cardiovascular disease mortality: insights from a device-based prospective study
item.description: A prospective cohort study (64,743 UK Biobank participants) found that combinations of stepping intensity (peak 30-min cadence) and daily step counts (<5000, 5000-7500, 7500-10,000, >10,000 steps/day) were associated with different risks for all-cause and cardiovascular disease mortality, with 7500-10,000 steps/day at approximately 100 steps/min showing the lowest all-cause mortality risk (HR 0.57; 95% CI 0.47 to 0.69).
item.author: BJSM

item.title: Multidimensional evidence map of sport science and medicine research in highly trained, elite and world-class female athletes: a scoping review
item.description: A scoping review of 3,867 records (1970-2025) on sport science and medicine research in highly trained female athletes found increasing but persistent gaps in participant representation (31% female), geographical coverage, and health-related themes, with pelvic floor (26 studies), breast health (11 studies), and (peri-)menopause (2 studies) being least common.
item.author: BJSM

item.title: Combining three-dimensional ankle exercises with short-foot training improves proprioception and dynamic balance in female karatekas with flatfoot: A randomized controlled trial.
item.description: A randomized controlled trial (n=34) found that combining three-dimensional ankle exercises with short-foot training (SF-3DAE) led to greater improvements in navicular drop (2.24 mm vs 1.16 mm), ankle proprioception (3° vs 1.59° error), and dynamic balance (17.49% vs 7.82% Y-Balance total reach) compared to short-foot exercise (SFE) alone in female karate athletes with flatfoot.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Age, resilience, social support, and health literacy as predictors of functional ability in people with spinal cord injury: a 6-month follow-up study.
item.description: A 6-month follow-up study (n=367) on traumatic spinal cord injury patients found that younger age (β=-0.02), higher resilience (β=0.22), and higher health literacy (β=0.32) were significant independent predictors of greater functional ability (Modified Barthel Index) over time, despite only modest overall improvement in MBI scores (from 43.50 to 46.81).
item.author: PubMed
